units.section: How should the guidelines be used?
units.text: As a guiding principle, be transparent about your AI project and the tools, data and algorithms you will be using, working in the open where possible.
units.text_start: be transparent about your AI project and the tools, data and algorithms
units.text_end: working in the open where possible

units.section: 2. Make decisions in a diverse multidisciplinary team
units.text: Developing, evaluating and delivering AI projects will be more effective with diverse teams that understand the interdependent disciplines that AI technologies incorporate. Require the successful supplier(s) to assemble a team with the right skill sets, and to address the need for diversity to mitigate bias in the AI system.
units.text_start: Require the successful supplier(s) to assemble a team with the right skill sets
units.text_end: diversity to mitigate bias in the AI system

units.section: 3. Conduct a data assessment before starting your procurement process
units.text: Availability of relevant data is often a prerequisite for any AI system, so time should not be spent discussing AI procurement if no data will be available. Ensure data governance mechanisms are in place from the start of the procurement process. Assess whether relevant data will be available for the project.
units.text_start: time should not be spent discussing AI procurement if no data will be available
units.text_end: Assess whether relevant data will be available for the project

units.text: Ensure that a discovery into your data is conducted before you go to market. If a thorough assessment of the data proves difficult or has not been made, make it a requirement in the invitation-to-tender to conduct a comprehensive check of the data the AI system will use to base its decisions upon.
units.text_start: a discovery into your data is conducted before you go to market
units.text_end: comprehensive check of the data the AI system will use

units.text: Your AI impact assessment should be initiated at the project design stage. Your AI impact assessment should outline: user needs and public benefit; human and socio-economic impacts; consequences for existing technical and procedural landscape; data quality and any potential inaccuracy or bias; any potential unintended consequences; whole-of-life cost considerations.
units.text_start: Your AI impact assessment should be initiated at the project design stage
units.text_end: whole-of-life cost considerations, including ongoing support and maintenance requirements

units.section: 4. Assess the benefits and risks of AI deployment
units.text: Explain in your procurement documentation that the public benefit is a main driver of your decision-making process when assessing proposals. Set out clearly in your procurement documentation why you consider AI to be relevant to the problem, and be open to alternative solutions. Conduct initial AI impact assessments at the start of the procurement process.
units.text_start: the public benefit is a main driver of your decision-making process
units.text_end: Conduct initial AI impact assessments at the start of the procurement process

units.section: 5. Engage effectively with the market from the outset
units.text: Engage with AI suppliers early and within your planning phase. Reach out in various ways to a wide variety of AI suppliers. Encourage an open environment that supports competition in the AI ecosystem. All preliminary market engagement must observe the principles of public procurement and be handled in such a way that no supplier gains a preferential advantage.
units.text_start: Engage with AI suppliers early and within your planning phase
units.text_end: no supplier gains a preferential advantage

units.section: 6. Establish the right route to market and focus on the challenge rather than a specific solution
units.text: Provide a clear problem statement, rather than detailed specifications for a solution. Tell suppliers about the situation or challenge, and let them propose a solution that meets your needs. Prioritise an iterative approach to product development and reflect this accordingly in the invitation to tender.
units.text_start: Provide a clear problem statement, rather than detailed specifications for a solution
units.text_end: reflect this accordingly in the invitation to tender

units.text: There are currently a number of routes to market to purchase AI systems. Framework agreements including G-Cloud, Digital Outcomes and Specialists, and the Spark Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) are useful starting points. Innovation-oriented procedures can include agile procurement with proof-of-concepts, technology contests such as GovTech Catalyst, Innovation Partnerships, and specialist AI DPS from Crown Commercial Service.
units.text_start: Framework agreements including G-Cloud, Digital Outcomes and Specialists
units.text_end: Dynamic Purchasing System for AI from Crown Commercial Service

units.text: Use output-based requirements in your invitation-to-tender that focus on describing the challenges and opportunities you are facing. This will allow suppliers to determine which technologies are most appropriate for your requirements.
units.text_start: Use output-based requirements in your invitation-to-tender
units.text_end: which technologies are most appropriate for your requirements

units.section: 8. Avoid Black Box algorithms and vendor lock in
units.text: Encourage explainability and interpretability of algorithms and make this one of your design criteria. This means using methods and techniques that allow the results to be understood by your team. Highly ‘explainable’ outputs from your AI system will be able to be interpreted by your team, and by other suppliers. This will also make it more likely for you to be able to engage with other suppliers to continue or build upon your AI system in the future, limiting the risk of vendor lock-in.
units.text_start: Encourage explainability and interpretability of algorithms
units.text_end: limiting the risk of vendor lock-in

units.text: Robust practices may include: Having an internal AI ethics approach; Processes to ensure accountability over outputs of algorithms; Avoiding outputs that could be unfairly discriminatory; Designing for reproducibility; Testing the model under a range of conditions; Defining acceptable model performance; Robust and proportionate security provision. Also review the specialist skills, qualifications and diversity of the team.
units.text_start: Having an internal AI ethics approach
units.text_end: diversity of the team that will develop and deploy the AI system

units.section: 10. Consider the lifecycle management of the AI system
units.text: Consider during AI procurement that lifespan testing, not a one-time decision, is required. Ensure that knowledge transfer and training is part of your requirement. Ensure that you make training and explanations for non-specialists that might need to understand the AI system part of your requirement. Ensure you have the appropriate ongoing support and hosting arrangements in place.
units.text_start: lifespan testing, not a one-time decision, is required
units.text_end: ongoing support and hosting arrangements in place

units.text: Testing the model on an ongoing basis is necessary to maintain its accuracy. Therefore, establish with the supplier how the efficacy of the model will be monitored once deployed.
units.text_start: Testing the model on an ongoing basis is necessary to maintain its accuracy
units.text_end: how the efficacy of the model will be monitored once deployed

units.text: Consider what the end-of-life processes for your AI system and the data should look like. Defining end-of-contract roles and processes for both the contracting authority and the supplier is important. Ensure the contract includes such considerations.
units.text_start: end-of-life processes for your AI system and the data
units.text_end: Ensure the contract includes such considerations

units.section: AI-specific considerations within the procurement process
units.text: As a general principle any AI procurement should be investigated with the mindset of “how could AI technologies potentially benefit us?” rather than “how can we make our problem fit an AI system solution?”.
units.text_start: how could AI technologies potentially benefit us
units.text_end: how can we make our problem fit an AI system solution
